profile.headline: Software Engineer at Burro
profile.summary: Graduating in May 2020, most of my engineering experience is non professional. It began with a robotics club in High School and continued with assignments in college, as well as projects which didn't bear fruit. For example, a modular solar power system I worked on as part of a group for Engineers Without Borders. My interests lie in robotics, especially controls and embedded systems, and I have experience with planning, RTOS, concurrency, and distributed systems as well.

positions.title: Head Teaching Assistant
positions.description: Head lab teaching assistant for ESE 112, physics E&M. I was in charge of managing other lab TAs, running labs, and grading lab reports. For the fall semester I also led recitation.

positions.title: Teaching Assistant
positions.description: Lab Teaching Assistant for ESE 112, Physics E&M and ESE 215, Intro Circuits. I helped run labs and grade reports. I also helped proctor and grade exams.

honors.title: Berkman Opportunity Fund Recipient
honors.description: The Berkman Fund provides awards of $500 to $1000 to support student ideas that might lead to innovative products and companies. The reward must be used for product development, including materials, components, lab fees, etc. The funds cannot be used for legal or professional fees and recipients must provide reports on the use of the funds and outcomes. My senior design team applied for this grant for our capstone project: https://devpost.com/software/ver.
